sensitiveBoundaries: flagged — command execution, filesystem and protected-state authority, path handling, JSON/deserialization boundaries, raw Agent output, and harness result attribution
codebaseConstraints: Conform to Loom's functional-core/imperative-shell, readonly discriminated-union, typed-reducer, parse-don't-validate, fail-closed, and exact-roster/slot patterns. Extend the existing domain-specific seams in `engine/src/core/panel-kernel.ts`, `engine/src/core/panel-program.ts`, `engine/src/core/standalone-review.ts`, `engine/src/core/review-panel.ts`, and Wave Gate core checks; keep architecture panel, Refutation Panel, Wave Gate, and Standalone Review as separate typed domain programs rather than a generic workflow abstraction. Preserve `engine/src/state-manager.ts` and existing hook authority as the only protected State File writer; use existing no-follow, run-boundary, atomic-publication, immutable-artifact, model/Skill-gate, Pi adapter, and Claude Code adapter conventions. Preserve Pi and Claude Code behavior and canonical run artifacts. Existing helper commands remain temporary compatibility adapters during incremental migration. Treat `/home/peterstorm/dev/agentic/fugue` as current architecture context, but do not assume capabilities its local APIs do not provide.
errorHandlingPhilosophy: Either/Result-style typed errors throughout the functional core, with exceptions caught and translated only at filesystem, process, CLI, and harness boundaries; retries are explicit bounded program state and failures remain fail-closed
concurrencyAndState: persistent, crash-resumable, audited program state; asynchronous semantic Agent fan-out may complete out of order, while request/slot acceptance, replay, next-action derivation, and terminal outcomes remain deterministic, idempotent, monotonic, and strongly consistent under Loom's single-writer authority; no distributed state by default
dataAndPersistence: Reuse existing protected JSON state and run-scoped JSON/Markdown artifact storage unless the design demonstrates a concrete need otherwise. Migrate incrementally without discarding existing runs or in-flight authority; preserve immutable accepted history and raw transcripts until explicit operator cleanup, with atomic publication and recoverable interruption semantics.
techPreferences: Prefer the existing TypeScript/Bun stack, readonly ADTs, branded identities, `ts-pattern`, typed reducers, Result/Either composition, fast-check property tests, and thin I/O ports/adapters. Use substantially more of Fugue's real shipped pipeline/runtime capabilities where they fit, including static typed DAGs, conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in waves, deterministic state-machine transitions, `JobLike`/replay seams, HITL suspension, capability scoping, and tracing. Do not invent or rely on Fugue agent-call nodes, nested subgraphs, bounded cross-node loops, or dynamic fan-out; the local codebase currently lacks them. Avoid a generic workflow DSL, a new runtime service, and prompt- or shell-owned deterministic orchestration.
observability: Persist event/action audit visibility sufficient to inspect complete run history, issued request-to-result bindings, model and Agent attribution, slot attempts and retry consumption, accepted/rejected evidence, blocked reasons and recovery actions, Finding dispositions, publications, and terminal decisions. Preserve machine-readable status and benchmark metrics for parent command-character/tool-call reductions, plus Pi/Claude Code outcome parity; retain tracing where Fugue executes pipeline nodes.
backwardsCompatibility: Incremental brownfield migration must preserve Pi and Claude Code behavior, existing run artifacts and in-flight data, protected-state authority, evidence semantics, model/Skill gates, and current command outcomes. Keep existing helper commands as temporary adapters until the engine-owned interface proves replay and cross-harness parity; do not require a flag or cut-over that invalidates historical runs.
deployment: Ship inside the existing Loom TypeScript/Bun package and its Pi and Claude Code harness integrations. Add no infrastructure dependency, Redis/BullMQ deployment, database, queue, daemon, or runtime service by default; use existing JSON/run storage. Any Fugue use must be compatible with this constraint and with the APIs actually present in the evaluated local Fugue repository.
outOfScope: No replacement of semantic implementation, review, refutation, architecture choice, remediation judgment, advisory triage, or user policy decisions; no invisible semantic Agent spawning; no generic workflow DSL or generic domain program; no merging architecture and refutation lens vocabularies; no weakened Review Packet, run identity, exact-roster/slot, Finding, threshold, provenance, model/Skill, or fail-closed invariants; no parent-authored Finding sets, raw-evidence reconstruction, or canonical-slot selection; no relocation of deterministic orchestration into prompts, runbooks, or shell scripts; no second protected State File writer; no automatic historical cleanup; no unrestricted remediation or staging; and no pretending Fugue's missing agent-call, nested-subgraph, bounded-loop, or dynamic-fan-out features exist.
